scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

Do you think being surrounded by the same religious community like that changes how people see things?

Being part of a consistent religious community, such as attending Friday prayers at the same mosque with the same people, significantly influences one's perspective in several ways: 1. **Reinforcement of Beliefs**: The repetitive exposure to similar opinions and values within the community can reinforce existing beliefs, making them more ingrained and less likely to be questioned. 2. **Moral Framework**: The environment of the mosque, which includes teachings and community events, shapes a moral framework. For instance, emphasizing charity can prioritize such values in daily life. 3. **Diversity of Opinions**: While the community may share similar views, the lack of diverse perspectives can limit exposure to alternative viewpoints, potentially hindering critical thinking. However, a supportive community can foster confidence in shared values. 4. **Influence of Leaders**: Religious leaders play a crucial role in shaping beliefs. Their emphasis on certain practices can influence their perceived importance and interactions with others outside the community. 5. **Questioning Beliefs**: A community that discourages dissent may limit the exploration of other viewpoints, leading to a homogeneous belief system. Conversely, a community that encourages learning can foster a nuanced perspective. 6. **Long-term Effects**: Consistent exposure to the same environment can solidify beliefs, providing a strong moral compass but potentially hindering adaptability to new information. In conclusion, while being part of a religious community reinforces values and provides support, it is essential to seek diverse perspectives to maintain a balanced and critically thinking mindset.
